doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Practice, the road and Dizzy's death
title: Promoters see dollar signs; Stan Getz's light schedule
summary: Promoters ignore the toll, whereas Stan Getz had days off between gigs; he links this to Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Be nice if the promoters, producers, and everybody could understand.
Well, they don't understand 'cause all they see are dollar signs.

They -- but it would be nice if like -- Stan Getz had the thing going for him, man, like, he would go play one gig, then he'd have two days off. He'd play another gig, there'd be 3 days off. And the guy would still be getting paid. That was nice.
How'd he manage to do that?
That's Stan Getz. Remember what I said about Dizzy?
Stan Getz. They were different, you know. [laughs]
And I hate to, you know, I hate to say that, but it is. People would just face up to the reality and then say "That's life", but we have to remember that now and, you know, bend. But. Yeah. [laughs]
